name: Gong Zizhen
credit: Portrait of Gong Zizhen, Qing dynasty likeness · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Gong Zizhen (1792–1841), also known as Gong Dingan, was a Qing scholar-official and poet from Hangzhou. Trained in the New Text school of Confucian learning, he served in Beijing as a minor official and wrote sharply on the abuses of his age, urging reform of government and the recruitment of talent from beyond the usual channels.

In 1839 he left the capital and travelled south, writing as he went the 315 quatrains of his Ji hai za shi (Miscellaneous Poems of the Ji-hai Year). The sequence mixes farewell, memory and political feeling, and has long been counted among the best-known poems of the late Qing.

poems.title: 己亥雜詩 其五 (Ji hai za shi qi wu)
poems.author: Gong Zizhen
poems.text:
浩蕩離愁白日斜，吟鞭東指即天涯。
落紅不是無情物，化作春泥更護花。

poems.title: 己亥雜詩 其一百二十五 (Ji hai za shi qi yi bai er shi wu)
poems.author: Gong Zizhen
poems.text:
九州生氣恃風雷，萬馬齊瘖究可哀。
我勸天公重抖擻，不拘一格降人材。
